<description>
This PR fixes the `interface_ipc*.py` tests, which have been [failing](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35037#issuecomment-6082043240) on NetBSD since https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35037.

As file descriptor budget regressions of this kind recur (see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31537 and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36078), the macOS CI job now models NetBSD's limit so they are caught before merging rather than by nightly NetBSD CI afterwards.

See the commit messages for details.
</description>

[2026-10-28] c:6460646505 comment by Sjors (member):
Concept ACK

But `wrap-fd-limit.sh‎` in 311bc7c3bb274c7065f871198fa0910c205b8a6a loses our coverage for "infinite" file descriptors introduced by #34937.

We could run `feature_init.py` both capped and uncapped:

```diff
diff --git a/ci/test/03_test_script.sh b/ci/test/03_test_script.sh
index d5981147f4..1468638690 100755
--- a/ci/test/03_test_script.sh
+++ b/ci/test/03_test_script.sh
@@ -161,5 +161,6 @@ if [ -n "${CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT}" ]; then
   # Only the node processes are capped (via BITCOIN_CMD), not the Python
   # test runner, which needs more descriptors when running jobs in parallel.
-  export BITCOIN_CMD="${BASE_ROOT_DIR}/ci/test/wrap-fd-limit.sh ${BITCOIN_CMD:-bitcoin}"
+  BITCOIN_CMD_UNCAPPED="${BITCOIN_CMD:-bitcoin}"
+  export BITCOIN_CMD="${BASE_ROOT_DIR}/ci/test/wrap-fd-limit.sh ${BITCOIN_CMD_UNCAPPED}"
 fi

@@ -208,4 +209,20 @@ if [ "$RUN_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS" = "true" ]; then
     --quiet \
     --failfast
+
+  if [ -n "${CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT}" ]; then
+    # The capped suite also runs feature_init.py, but the wrapper overrides the
+    # RLIM_INFINITY and above-INT_MAX limits it tests. Repeat it without the cap.
+    BITCOIN_CMD="${BITCOIN_CMD_UNCAPPED}" \
+    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${DEPENDS_DIR}/${HOST}/lib" \
+    "${BASE_BUILD_DIR}/test/functional/test_runner.py" \
+      "${MAKEJOBS}" \
+      --tmpdirprefix "${BASE_SCRATCH_DIR}/test_runner_uncapped/" \
+      --ansi \
+      --combinedlogslen=99999999 \
+      --timeout-factor="${TEST_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_FACTOR}" \
+      --quiet \
+      --failfast \
+      feature_init.py
+  fi
 fi
```

Alternatively we could drop that test.
